title: Data Lakehouse
summary: A lakehouse puts warehouse-style tables on top of cheap object storage. Data lives as open Parquet files in S3, and a table format such as Apache Iceberg adds a metadata layer that tracks exactly which files make up each version of a table. That gives atomic commits, schema evolution, and time travel, and lets many engines (Spark, Trino, Snowflake, Python) safely read and write the same tables without copying data.

walkthrough.title: Ingest from sources
walkthrough.text: Change data capture from production databases, event streams, and SaaS exports flow into ingestion jobs every few minutes.

walkthrough.title: Write Parquet data files
walkthrough.text: The job writes new immutable Parquet files to object storage, organised by partition such as event date. Nothing existing is modified in place.

walkthrough.title: Commit a new snapshot atomically
walkthrough.text: The job writes new manifest files listing the data files, then asks the catalog to swap the table's current-metadata pointer with compare-and-swap. Readers see all of the commit or none of it.

walkthrough.title: Plan a query from metadata
walkthrough.text: Trino asks the catalog for the table's current snapshot. Using per-file min/max statistics in the manifests, it skips files that cannot match WHERE order_date = '2026-11-01'.

walkthrough.title: Read only what is needed
walkthrough.text: Workers read just the surviving files, and only the needed columns, in parallel straight from object storage.

walkthrough.title: Serve BI and ML from the same tables
walkthrough.text: Dashboards, notebooks, and training jobs all read the same governed tables, with no exports or copies.

walkthrough.title: Compact and expire
walkthrough.text: Maintenance jobs rewrite many small files into larger ones and expire old snapshots after the time-travel window, deleting files no snapshot references.

data.label: Sources
responsibilities: Produce the raw data the lakehouse organises.
Expose changes incrementally rather than full dumps.
Publish schemas and data contracts.

failureModes.impact: Ingestion fails or silently drops columns.
failureModes.mitigation: Data contracts; schema evolution rules; alerting.

data.label: Ingestion Jobs
responsibilities: Writes data files and commits them atomically.
Applies upserts and deletes (merge-on-read or copy-on-write).
Retries commits that conflict with concurrent writers.

failureModes.scenario: Job crashes after writing files, before commit
failureModes.impact: Orphan files take up space (but readers are unaffected).
failureModes.mitigation: Orphan-file cleanup; the commit is all-or-nothing.
Optimistic concurrency: retry on a fresh snapshot if files do not overlap.

data.label: Catalog & Table Metadata
responsibilities: Points each table name to its current metadata file.
Makes commits atomic with compare-and-swap.
Enforces access control and keeps schema history.

failureModes.impact: No new commits or query planning.
failureModes.mitigation: Highly available catalog service; data files remain safe in storage.

failureModes.impact: Split-brain views of the same table.
failureModes.mitigation: One shared catalog for all engines.

data.label: Object Storage
responsibilities: Stores all table data cheaply and durably.
Scales reads across thousands of parallel workers.
Separates storage from compute so each scales independently.

failureModes.scenario: Request rate limits on one prefix
failureModes.mitigation: Spread files across prefixes; fewer, larger files.
Versioning, object lock, and cross-region replication.

data.label: Query Engines

output.name: Results
output.type: Rows, after pruning files with metadata

responsibilities: Plan queries from metadata, skipping irrelevant files.
Read columns in parallel directly from storage.
Run maintenance: compaction and snapshot expiry.

failureModes.scenario: No partition or column stats to prune with
failureModes.impact: Full scans of terabytes for small queries.
failureModes.mitigation: Good partitioning, sort order, and file statistics.

data.label: BI & SQL Users
responsibilities: Build reports and business metrics.
Transform raw tables into modelled ones with dbt.
Use time travel to reproduce past numbers.

failureModes.mitigation: Resource groups, quotas, and query timeouts.

data.label: ML & Notebooks

input.name: Tables
input.type: Same tables, read by snapshot ID

responsibilities: Read the same tables as BI, no exports.
Pin snapshot IDs so training data is reproducible.
Write features back as new tables.

failureModes.mitigation: Tag snapshots used for training to exempt them from expiry.
Access through the catalog with column-level permissions.
